tutorial.title: PATCH Requests
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to use a PATCH request to send data to a server

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent:
PATCH is an HTTP method used to make partial updates to an existing resource, sending only the changes instead of the full data.

Unlike PUT, which replaces the entire resource, PATCH modifies only the specified fields.

lessons.title: PUT
lessons.interactiveContent:
PATCH is a request method that we use to update existing data on the server, like modifying an existing course Mimo wants to revise.

Make sure to pick PATCH.
lessons.hardModeContent:
PATCH updates selected fields of existing data, like modifying a course Mimo wants to revise.

Change only selected fields of course 10, keeping the other fields unchanged.

Make sure to pick PATCH, followed by /courses, and finally /10.

lessons.title: PUT URL
lessons.interactiveContent:
PATCH relies on a URL containing the server address, along with the type of resource the new data is related to.

Make sure to pick mimo.org.
lessons.hardModeContent:
PATCH relies on a URL containing the server address, along with the type of resource the new data is related to.

Use HTTPS to target course 10 on the server mimo.org.

Make sure to pick https://, followed by mimo.org.

lessons.interactiveContent:
This PATCH request's URL shows that an existing course should be updated under courses.

Make sure to pick /courses, followed by /10.
lessons.hardModeContent:
This PATCH request's URL shows that an existing course should be updated under courses.

Complete the resource path for course 10.

lessons.title: PUT URL Query Parameters
lessons.interactiveContent:
In a PATCH request, the payload contains only the specific changes, updating parts of the resource without replacing the entire content.

We send only the specific changes to the resource, meaning missing fields remain unchanged.

Make sure to pick {, followed by }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In a PATCH request, the payload contains only the specific changes, updating parts of the resource without replacing the entire content.

You send only the specific changes to the resource, meaning missing fields remain unchanged.

Change only the course title to TypeScript in a JSON object.

Make sure to pick {, followed by "title", "TypeScript", and finally }.

lessons.title: Question: PUT
lessons.interactiveContent:
What do we use PATCH requests for?

For updating an existing data on the serverFor retrieving data from the server

For updating an existing data on the server.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We use PATCH requests to update existing data on a server.

Course 10 already exists. A PATCH request sends only its new title. What should happen?

Course 10's title changes while its other data remainsA second course is created because sending data always creates a resourceCourse 10 is only retrieved because requests to existing URLs cannot update data

Course 10's title changes while its other data remains.

lessons.title: Question: PUT URL
lessons.interactiveContent:
How does the browser know where to send the data in the PATCH request?

Through the server address in the request's URLBy reading the data that the request is sending

Through the server address in the request's URL.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A request starts with PATCH https://api.mimo.org/users/7. Which part tells the browser which server receives the data?

api.mimo.org in the request URLusers in the path, because it names the serverThe JSON field in the body, because its name selects the server

api.mimo.org in the request URL.

lessons.title: Question: PUT URL 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Looking at this URL, what might the data we're sending be related to?

An update to an existing article A new article submitted by someone

An update to an existing article.
lessons.hardModeContent:
What should the shown request do if article 458 already exists?

Update article 458's title to UFOs sighted [Revised]Create a new article and assign it the next available IDUpdate the title of every article because the body has no article ID

Update article 458's title to UFOs sighted [Revised].

lessons.hardModeContent:

Make sure to pick PATCH, followed by article, and finally 112.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
In a PATCH request, do you send only the data you want to change or the entire updated resource?

You only send the data you want to changeYou send the entire updated resource

You only send the data you want to change.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A course has a title, description, and duration. You want a PATCH request to change only its title. What should the payload contain?

Only the new title valueThe title, description, and duration, because omitted fields are deletedNo payload, because the server reads the new title from the URL

Make sure to pick Only the new title value.

lessons.title: PUT Body
lessons.interactiveContent:
PATCH requests look very similar to PUT requests in Express.

Make sure to pick patch.
lessons.hardModeContent:
PATCH requests look very similar to PUT requests in Express.

Register an update handler for /users.

Make sure to pick app, followed by ., and finally patch.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
Like with PUT requests, we define the endpoint for PATCH requests and specify which resource should be updated via route parameters.

Make sure to pick / followed by users and then /, :id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Like with PUT requests, we define the endpoint for PATCH requests and specify which resource should be updated via route parameters.

Complete the route for one user identified by id.

Make sure to pick /, followed by users, /, and finally :id.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
PATCH requests often rely on route parameters to identify the specific resource that should be updated.

We use req.params.id to unpack a route parameter with the name id.

Make sure to pick req followed by . and then params, ., id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
PATCH requests often rely on route parameters to identify the specific resource that should be updated.

Use req.params with the parameter name shown in the route.

Read the user ID from the route parameters.

Make sure to pick req, followed by ., params, ., and finally id.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Like PUT requests, PATCH requests also contain data in their request body.

In a PATCH request, we only send specific changes to the resource, meaning missing fields remain unchanged.

Make sure to pick req, followed by .body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Like PUT requests, PATCH requests also contain data in their request body.

In a PATCH request, you send only specific changes to the resource, so missing fields remain unchanged.

Store the parsed request body in requestData.

Make sure to pick req, followed by .body.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
To allow accessing the body, we need to tell our express app to use express.json, a built-in middleware.

Make sure to pick express.json().
lessons.hardModeContent:
To access JSON request bodies, configure your Express app with the built-in express.json middleware.

Register the JSON parser before the update route.

Make sure to pick app, followed by use, and finally express.json().

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we want to access the passed data, we parse it. As soon as we've done that, we can access and work with the data in the request body.

Notice that it's common for not all possible fields to be provided when using PATCH requests.

Make sure to pick username, followed by email.
lessons.hardModeContent:
After parsing a request body, you can access and use its data.

Notice that it's common for not all possible fields to be provided when using PATCH requests.

Read the supplied username and the optional email field.

Make sure to pick username, followed by email.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Similar to other methods, we can and should send back a response.

Make sure to pick res, followed by ., and finally send.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Similar to other methods, we can and should send back a response.

Send the update confirmation to the client.

Make sure to pick res, followed by ., and finally send.

lessons.title: PUT Body 2 - Copy -  - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
The default status if everything goes according to plan and a new element is created or added to the database is 200 OK.

Make sure to pick . followed by status(200) and then ., send.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The default status if everything goes according to plan and a new element is created or added to the database is 200 OK.

Respond with the successful update status and confirmation.

Make sure to pick ., followed by status(200), ., and finally send.

lessons.title: PUT Headers
lessons.interactiveContent:
A PATCH request has headers providing extra context, like Content-Type, which tells us the format of the request body.

Make sure to pick Content-Type:, followed by application/json.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A PATCH request has headers providing extra context, like Content-Type, which tells us the format of the request body.

Declare that the update body uses JSON.

Make sure to pick Content-Type:, followed by application/json.

lessons.title: PUT Headers 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
You can see that this PATCH request's body Content-Type is application/json, the most common content type.

Make sure to pick application, followed by /, and finally json.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Set Content-Type to match the shown JSON request body.

Make sure to pick application, followed by /, and finally json.

lessons.title: Question: PUT Body
lessons.interactiveContent:
Where do PATCH requests store the data they send to the server?

In the request bodyOnly in the URL, as query parameter values

In the request body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You send a PATCH request to change user 937's username. Where should the JSON containing the new username go?

In the request bodyIn the URL path after /users/937In the Content-Type header instead of the body

Make sure to pick In the request body.

Use a route parameter to target the user being updated.

Make sure to pick app, followed by ., patch, and finally "/users/:id".

JSONHTTP

JSONHTTP, because PATCH is an HTTP methodA URL query, because the username is a key-value pair

lessons.title: Question: POST Headers 2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does a PATCH request's Content-Type header tell us?

The format (JSON) of the data we're sending to the serverThe format of the data in the server's database

The format (JSON) of the data we're sending to the server.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The shown request declares Content-Type: application/json. What does that tell the server about the body?
